To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
TRACK and M-TRACK are the first contemporary sink models that can achieve significant improvements in WSN lifetime longevity by exploiting the CDS property of the network graph.
TRACK and M-TRACK, our novel sink mobility models for WSNs, can extend WSN lifetime by 2.4 times and 7.3 times, respectively.
TRACK and M-TRACK, our proposed sink mobility models, are the first contemporary models that can extend WSN lifetime and secure data aggregation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a sink mobility model which can prolong WSN lifetime, while ensuring that the data aggregation is secure and efficient.
the design and analysis of a new sink mobility model that can be applied to a variety of WSN applications.
the design of a novel sink mobility scheme that can significantly extend the network lifetime of wireless sensor networks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the TRACK and M-TRACK models are the most efficient, robust and secure mobility models proposed to date.
the TRACK model is a novel, efficient, secure and robust sink mobility model for WSNs that can significantly extend WSN lifetime.
TRACK is an energy efficient and secure sink mobility model that can be easily implemented and deployed in real world WSNs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TRACK can be used as an alternative to static sinks in a WSN and M-TRACK as an extension to TRACK, to achieve even better WSN lifetime.

TRACK is the only model which can achieve the following objectives in a WSN simultaneously: (1) it extends the WSN lifetime, (2) it reduces the delay between consecutive visits of the sink to the nodes in the network, (3) it reduces the routing overhead, (4) it improves the data aggregation security, and (5) it does not require any additional hardware or infrastructure.
TRACK, by its very definition, is a novel, efficient, and robust sink mobility model that can extend the WNS lifetime and secure data aggregation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CDS property of the underlying network graph can be exploited to design efficient sink mobility models.
TRACK and M-TRACK can be used as an alternative to existing sink mobility models, especially when the sink mobility is not a feasible option.
TRACK and M-TRACK are the first sink mobility models that exploit the CDS-MT framework for WSN longevity and secure data gathering.
